slice: PAWA-2 — the juul ledger · PAWA-3 — the out-of-pawa gate clause
phase: R2-with-a-reference-concept — `PawaLedger` exists in Python but its `charge()` has zero callers, and the live `deduct()` path charges the wrong number
authored_from: Pawa §2 (juul as the unit of account; balance ← balance − pawa, admitted only if balance ≥ pawa); reconciled against apps/api/sustena/core/pawa.py
note: Two slices in one file, because the second is the first's only real consumer. PAWA-2 is the balance PAWA-1's readings are charged against; PAWA-3 is the conjunct that refuses a run nobody can afford. Still internal accounting throughout: the clause refuses a run, it moves no real value.
★★★_the_hard_boundary_and_it_is_ADR_0001: A juul balance is an INTERNAL ACCOUNTING FACT ON A SINGLE HOST — never real money, never a transferable asset, never a payment rail. Issuing a real, public, transferable token is a DISTINCT, LATER, HUMAN-AUTHORISED ACT and is out of scope. ★★ Here that is STRUCTURAL rather than promised: the module has NO TRANSFER (no method moves juul between principals; a charge has no counterparty at all), NO MINT (nothing creates juul except `credit`, which DECLARES a starting balance and is deliberately named apart from a debit — genesis is PAWA-7 and issuance PAWA-8), and NO RAIL (no I/O anywhere, by ADR-0001). A test asserts that charging one principal leaves every other balance untouched — because there is nothing that could move it.

★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★★_1_there_is_no_juul_ledger_in_Rust_an: Grep-confirmed before building. `approval::NonceLedger` records SPENT APPROVAL-TOKEN NONCES (single-use redemption at the gate) and `consensus::Ledger` is a PAXOS ACCEPTOR SET. Neither is a balance, and conflating any of the three would be a genuine confusion — hence `JuulLedger`, the thirty-seventh collision, with the newcomer taking the longer name.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★★_2_a_PawaReading_is_what_a_debit_CONS: PAWA-1 shipped `PawaReading` with NO PUBLIC CONSTRUCTOR — the only source is `pawa::meter` over an `Execution` that COMMITTED. So `charge(&PawaReading)` means a debit is always backed by a real, measured, genuinely-committed run. THERE IS NO `debit(amount)` IN THIS MODULE: a charge cannot be invented, and a caller wanting to spend juul must first have done work that cost it. This is the structural question the PAWA-1 report left open, answered by the signature rather than by a check.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★_3_the_affordability_rule_here_is_the_: `charge` returns `Insufficient` when the balance will not cover the reading. That is the ledger's own answer about its own balance. The GATE CLAUSE that refuses an operator RUN on insufficient balance — `admit = guard ∧ constraints ∧ token_ok ∧ balance ≥ pawa` — is PAWA-3 and is NOT this slice. Nothing here is wired into `execute_admitted`.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★★_4_PAWA_3_the_candidate_ALREADY_EXIST: Confirmed in `execute_admitted` before designing anything. The gate applies the effect to a COPY (`let mut working = State::new(state.clone())`), then takes `let candidate = working.snapshot()` and checks closure, the invariants, the post-conditions, `D` and `F` against it — so by the time the commit block is reached, the candidate's MUTATIONS AND EVENTS ALREADY EXIST. They had to: `D` is evaluated over the (before, after) pair and `F` over the declared movements. THE RUN'S REAL COST IS THEREFORE KNOWABLE AT GATE TIME AT NO EXTRA WORK, and `candidate_pawa` returns exactly the number the committed `PawaReading` will carry — asserted equal, not assumed.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★★_5_PAWA_3_priced_against_the_MEASUREM: `meta.pawa_cost` is NOT consulted by the clause. Pricing against it is the reference's own wrong path — PAWA-2's STEP-0 found `deduct()` charging exactly that, and it is `0` for every operator that calls it, so an estimate-priced clause NEVER REFUSES. The affordability conjunct reads `candidate_pawa`, the real measured cost, and a dedicated test funds a principal with HALF THE REAL COST while the declared estimate is `0` — an estimate-priced gate would admit it; this one refuses.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★_6_PAWA_3_where_the_conjunct_SITS_and_: Last before commit, and specifically BEFORE the token redemption. Two reasons, both real: the candidate does not exist earlier (so the cost is not knowable), and being turned back on cost must leave an approval UNSPENT — the same courtesy `execute_admitted`'s own comment already grants an invariant refusal ('being turned back by an invariant should leave the person free to fix the state and use the same approval, not burn it').

divergence.statement: The LEDGER CONCEPT exists in Python (`core/pawa.py::PawaLedger`) but the piece PAWA-2 is about is not in force there — and reconciling it turned up a finding the brief did not have.
divergence.★★★_the_finding_the_reference's_LIVE_deb: The brief said `charge()` is scaffolded with zero callers, and that is exactly right — grep-confirmed, its only other mention in the whole reference is a docstring. BUT `deduct()`, the method `charge()` itself calls, HAS FOUR REAL CALLERS: `budget.py`, `calendar.py`, `procurement.py` and `tasks.py` each call `ctx.pawa.deduct(...)` on every operator run. So the reference DOES have a wired debit path. ★★★ What it charges is `meta.pawa_cost` — THE AUTHOR'S STATIC DECLARED ESTIMATE — and every one of those operators declares `pawa_cost = 0`, so the live path debits nothing on every call. `budget.py`'s own docstring says so: *'For budget operators (pawa_cost=0) this is always a no-op ... The call is still made explicitly so the pattern is established for paid operators in later epics.'* ★★ That is PAWA-1's static-versus-measured split showing up as a real consequence: **the reference's live debit path is wired to the estimate, not to the measurement**, and the meter's readings — which are real and non-zero — reach no ledger at all. Naming it because it is precisely the wire this slice's `charge(&PawaReading)` signature makes impossible to get wrong.

★★_what_is_at_parity_and_what_is_the_sha.at parity — the concept: A per-principal balance, an insufficient-balance refusal that returns rather than raises (`deduct` returns `False`, `charge` returns `Insufficient`), and zero-cost calls succeeding trivially.
★★_what_is_at_parity_and_what_is_the_sha.★ at parity, and NOT this row's inventio: The reference's `get_balance` is ALREADY a fold: `select(func.sum(pawa_ledger.c.delta))` over an append-only delta table. Saying the fold-based balance is a Rust sharpening would have been wrong, and it is recorded here as parity.
★★_what_is_at_parity_and_what_is_the_sha.★★★ the sharpening — a debit backed by a: `deduct(user_id, sustain_id, amount: int, reason: str)` takes a BARE INTEGER: any caller can debit any amount for any stated reason. `charge(&PawaReading)` takes a value that cannot be constructed except by metering a committed run — so the amount, the principal, the operator and the sustain all come off the measurement and none can be supplied by the caller.
★★_what_is_at_parity_and_what_is_the_sha.★★ the sharpening — credit and debit are: The reference's ledger table is a signed `delta` column. Here `Entry::{Credit, Debit}` are distinct variants, so *where did this juul come from* stays answerable — and a debit carries the operator and sustain that incurred it, so it is traceable to its run.

divergence.★_what_is_deliberately_NOT_ported: `PawaLedger.charge()`'s 70/20/5/5 ROYALTY SPLIT is not here. That is MYC-5/PAWA-5's concern, it distributes to a contributor, a treasury, a referrer and a validator — every one of which is a TRANSFER — and this slice has no transfer by design. Porting it would have breached the hard boundary in the first module that touches a balance.
divergence.the_honest_limits: ★★ NOTHING IS WIRED INTO THE GATE — `execute_admitted` neither meters nor charges; PAWA-3 is the gate clause and it is the next row. ★★ `credit` IS AN UNGATED DECLARATION — any caller can declare any opening balance, because genesis (PAWA-7) and issuance (PAWA-8) are the rows that decide who may. It is named apart from a debit precisely so that gap is visible rather than hidden inside a signed number. ★ THE LEDGER IS IN-MEMORY — durable storage is the host's, exactly as the event log and the meter are; `with_entries` is the reload door, the same shape `NonceLedger::with_spent` uses. ★★ A CHARGE HAS NO COUNTERPARTY — spending REMOVES juul from circulation rather than moving it anywhere, which is a deliberate posture and is asserted; PAWA-6's treasury is where a destination would be introduced if one ever is. ★ BALANCES ARE `f64` — the meter produces a real-valued pawa, so the ledger matches it; a fixed-point or integer-minor-unit representation is a real decision that belongs with the calibration of κ, not before it. ★★ AND THERE IS NO REVOCATION OR REVERSAL — no method un-charges an entry, because the ledger is append-only; a correction would be a compensating entry, which is a row nobody has written yet. ★★ **PAWA-3's OWN LIMITS.** THE CHARGE CANNOT BE `Insufficient` BY CONSTRUCTION — the identical cost was checked against the identical balance a few lines above and nothing interleaves, so the return value of the commit-time `charge` is deliberately not re-handled; if that ever stops being true the equality test between candidate and reading is what would break first. ★★ THE LEDGER IS BORROWED MUTABLY FOR THE CALL — `Affordability::Metered` holds an `&mut JuulLedger`, so one call charges one ledger; concurrent or interleaved charging is a host concern, and this core has no threads (ADR-0001). ★ THE CLAUSE PRICES THE WHOLE RUN, NOT PER-NODE — a strategy walk (OPV-4) charges each node separately because each is its own `execute` call, which is right, but means a walk cannot be refused up-front on its TOTAL cost; a budget over a whole walk would be a further row. ★★ AND NOTHING CREDITS ANYONE — the debit still has no counterparty, so PAWA-3 changes nothing about the hard boundary: the clause refuses a run, it moves no value.
divergence.★★★_PAWA_3_the_reference_HAS_the_seam_bu: At parity: the seam itself. The reference's `_charge_pawa` runs on the write path and returns an `OperatorResult.fail('Insufficient pawa: ...')` when `deduct` reports False — so the SHAPE of an affordability refusal exists there, and this row did not invent it. ★★★ What it charges is `meta.pawa_cost`, and every operator that calls it declares `0`, so `deduct` returns True immediately for zero-cost calls and THE CLAUSE NEVER FIRES. `budget.py`'s own docstring says so: 'For budget operators (pawa_cost=0) this is always a no-op.' So the seam is at parity and the CORRECTNESS is rust-ahead: the conjunct here prices the measurement, which the candidate makes free to compute, and therefore actually refuses.
divergence.★★_PAWA_3_additive_and_opt_in_safe_by_th: `execute_admitted` and `execute` delegate to the new `execute_afforded` with `Affordability::Unmetered`, so EVERY caller written before PAWA-3 and every R1 parity vector behaves BYTE-FOR-BYTE as it did — asserted directly by running the same call both ways and comparing state and mutations. The same delegating shape `run → run_with_effect → run_under` used for the strategy walker. ★ And `Unmetered` is a VACUOUS clause, not a fail-closed one: a host that has not opted into an economy has not said everyone has zero juul, it has said there is no economy to price against — the same reading `Enforcement::enabled` gets for the invariant gate.

backing_cases.name: a_charge_is_always_backed_by_a_real_metered_run
backing_cases.why: ★★★ THE STRUCTURAL PROPERTY OF THIS SLICE. `charge` takes a `PawaReading`, and a `PawaReading` has no public constructor — the only source is `pawa::meter` over a COMMITTED execution. There is no `debit(amount)` anywhere in the module, so a charge cannot be invented, and the resulting debit carries the operator and sustain it came from.

backing_cases.name: a_run_is_charged_to_whoever_made_it
backing_cases.why: ★ The principal comes off the reading, not off an argument, so a caller cannot redirect the bill to somebody else. Another funded principal's balance is asserted untouched.

affordability_cases.name: a_charge_is_admitted_only_if_the_balance_covers_it
affordability_cases.why: ★★ `balance ← balance − pawa`, admitted only if `balance ≥ pawa` — the row's own rule, and the resulting balance is asserted to be exactly the difference rather than approximately it.

affordability_cases.name: an_unaffordable_charge_is_refused_and_the_balance_is_byte_identical
affordability_cases.why: ★★ An honest refusal, not an error: `Insufficient` carries both numbers so a caller can say HOW MUCH short. And the whole ledger is asserted BYTE-IDENTICAL afterwards — nothing was appended, which is the refusal-changes-nothing discipline every prior slice keeps.

affordability_cases.name: a_refused_charge_never_clamps_the_balance_to_zero
affordability_cases.why: ★ Clamping would silently lose the overspend AND report a debit that did not happen. The balance is asserted unchanged and the debit count zero — refusal is refusal, not a partial charge.

affordability_cases.name: a_balance_exactly_equal_to_the_cost_is_affordable
affordability_cases.why: The rule is `balance ≥ pawa`, not `>`. A balance that exactly covers a run is spent to zero, which is a real boundary worth pinning rather than leaving to the reader.

affordability_cases.name: an_unfunded_principal_starts_at_zero_and_cannot_spend
affordability_cases.why: ★ A principal with no entries has a balance of 0.0 — correctly, because that is a SUM OVER AN EMPTY SET rather than a claim about anything unmeasured — and therefore cannot afford a non-zero run.

fold_cases.name: the_balance_is_the_fold_of_the_entries_and_rebuilds_identically
fold_cases.why: ★★ The `state = fold(events)` discipline one layer up. There is NO STORED BALANCE FIELD that could drift — the fold IS the balance — so `rebuild` agreeing with `balance_of` is true by construction rather than kept true by care. The entry list is asserted append-only: one credit and three debits after three charges.

fold_cases.name: a_hosts_durable_entries_rebuild_the_same_balance
fold_cases.why: ★ The host holds durability, the core holds the decision — the same split `NonceLedger::with_spent` uses. A ledger reloaded from its own entries is asserted EQUAL to the original, so a host's round trip cannot silently change a balance.

boundary_cases.name: a_debit_reduces_circulation_and_creates_nothing
boundary_cases.why: ★ CONSERVATION, stated as the posture it is: a cost debit has NO COUNTERPARTY, so spending REMOVES juul from circulation rather than moving it to someone else. Total circulation is asserted to fall by exactly the pawa spent.

boundary_cases.name: a_credit_and_a_debit_are_different_entries_not_a_signed_number
boundary_cases.why: ★ So *where did this juul come from* stays answerable. The reference's table is a signed `delta` column; here the two are distinct variants, and `debits_of` returns only the debits — a credit is never counted as one.

boundary_cases.name: charging_one_principal_leaves_every_other_balance_untouched
boundary_cases.why: ★★★ THE HARD BOUNDARY, asserted: there is NO TRANSFER in this module. Nobody is credited by a charge, so no method here can move juul between principals — the other principal's balance is unchanged and circulation falls, rather than the juul appearing somewhere else.

gate_clause_cases.name: an_affordable_run_commits_and_is_charged_exactly_once
gate_clause_cases.why: ★★ The happy path end to end: the run commits, the ledger shows EXACTLY ONE debit (not zero, not two), the balance is the opening minus the real cost, and the fold still agrees with `balance_of` afterwards — so the debit went through the same append-only path every other entry does.

gate_clause_cases.name: an_unaffordable_run_is_refused_and_charges_nothing
gate_clause_cases.why: ★★★ THE WHOLE POINT: the gate stops the work BEFORE it costs anything. The refusal carries its own reason `insufficient_pawa` — distinct from guard, invariant, `D`, `F` and token refusals — and the LEDGER IS ASSERTED BYTE-IDENTICAL afterwards while the state is untouched and mutations and events are empty. *Refusal charges nothing* joins *refusal meters nothing* rather than contradicting it.

gate_clause_cases.name: it_prices_against_the_real_cost_not_the_declared_estimate
gate_clause_cases.why: ★★★ The reference's trap, made into a test. `budget.record_income` declares `pawa_cost = 0` — asserted — while its real metered cost is greater than zero — also asserted. A principal funded with HALF THE REAL COST would be admitted by an estimate-priced clause and is REFUSED here, which proves the conjunct reads the measurement and not the guess.

gate_clause_cases.name: the_candidate_price_equals_the_committed_readings_price
gate_clause_cases.why: ★★ Pre-commit affordability and the post-commit debit are THE SAME NUMBER, because both go through `compute_units`, `constraint_eval_count` and `storage_bytes`. Asserted rather than assumed — if they could differ, the gate would be admitting on one price and charging another.

gate_clause_cases.name: an_unmetered_call_behaves_exactly_as_before
gate_clause_cases.why: ★ ADDITIVE AND OPT-IN-SAFE. The same call run through `execute` and through `execute_afforded` with `Unmetered` produces byte-identical state and mutations, and commits despite no balance existing anywhere — because an absent ledger makes the clause VACUOUS rather than failing closed to broke.

gate_clause_cases.name: a_run_refused_by_an_earlier_conjunct_never_reaches_the_charge
gate_clause_cases.why: ★ The clause is the LAST before commit, so a guard refusal costs nothing either — the ledger is byte-identical after a run turned back by `params.amount > 0`. And `meter` would refuse to read an uncommitted execution regardless, so there are two independent reasons a refused run cannot be charged.
